paragraphs.text: We at Oceans Orthodontics and Pediatric Dentistry provide thoughtful, family-centered care with genuine warmth. Our team treats every patient with respect and attention so visits feel comfortable and personal.

Our goal is to make high-quality orthodontic and pediatric dental care accessible and stress-free. We tailor treatment plans to each child and family, focusing on long-term health, function, and confident smiles.
We offer specialty care across orthodontics and pediatric dentistry, using modern technology and evidence-based techniques to keep visits efficient and predictable.
From early pediatric visits to orthodontic consultations, we partner with families to educate, support, and deliver compassionate care so every patient can leave smiling.

Dr. Eric Frank, DDS, MA, MS is a board-certified orthodontist and Diplomate of the American Board of Orthodontics (ABO), achieving board certification in February 2015. He is committed to contemporary, evidence-based orthodontic care and continuing education.
Dr. Frank has presented research and stays active in professional organizations to bring advanced techniques, including Invisalign<sup>®</sup>, to his patients.

Dr. Frank graduated Phi Beta Kappa from the University of Florida (B.S., summa cum laude). He earned his D.D.S. at Columbia University College of Dental Medicine and completed orthodontic residency training at Columbia University Division of Orthodontics, where he served as Chief Resident.
He also earned an M.A. in Dental Education from Columbia University Teachers College and conducted craniofacial research while at Columbia.

Raised in South Florida and later living in New York City, Dr. Frank now calls Westfield home. He enjoys flying as a private pilot, competing in triathlons, scuba diving, skiing, and travel photography — many practice photos were taken by him.

image.alt: Dr. Eric Frank smiling in office

paragraphs.text: Dr. Aimee Leibowitz‑Frank, DDS is a board-certified pediatric dentist and Diplomate of the American Board of Pediatric Dentistry (ABPD). She brings specialized training in caring for children and patients with special health care needs.

Dr. Aimee earned her DDS from Columbia University College of Dental Medicine and completed a pediatric dentistry residency at Boston University. She is an active member of the American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry and other professional organizations.

Aimee loves working with children and focuses on making visits positive and accessible. She is fluent in Spanish, enjoys family time, scuba diving, yoga, and brings special training in treating children with sensory and developmental needs.
Tongue tie and airway-focused care credentials include LightScalpel laser provider training, Tongue Tied Academy courses, and additional airway education and affiliations with the Breathe Institute.

Dr. David Berkower, DDS is a pediatric dentist with training in hospital-based and clinical pediatric care. He completed a two-year pediatric dentistry residency and has experience in global health outreach treating children in underserved communities.

Dr. David earned his D.D.S. from Columbia University College of Dental Medicine after completing undergraduate studies at Yeshiva University. He served as chief resident during his pediatric residency.
Dr. David enjoys cooking, travel, concerts, and family time. His early global health experiences treating children helped shape his focus on compassionate pediatric care.

Dr. Ashley Wilmot, DMD is a pediatric dentist who completed specialty training and focuses on kindness, patience, and partnership with families to make dental visits positive and comfortable for children.

Dr. Ashley completed undergraduate studies at Hofstra University, a post‑baccalaureate program at Temple University Kornberg School of Dentistry, and received her D.M.D. from Tufts University School of Dental Medicine, followed by pediatric dentistry residency training.
Dr. Ashley enjoys travel, camping, hiking, pilates, and spending time with family. She has participated in international outreach dentistry and brings a calm, encouraging approach to young patients.

paragraphs.text: Comprehensive orthodontics covers a wide range of options — metal or ceramic braces, lingual braces, and clear aligners. Dr. Frank evaluates each patient’s bite, growth and goals, then presents treatment choices, risks and benefits so families can decide together.
InBrace places a custom Smartwire behind the teeth for discreet, continuous tooth movement. It’s an excellent option for patients who want brace-style results without visible brackets up front.

image.alt: Stylish teens smiling, discreet orthodontic treatment

paragraphs.text: Invisalign<sup>®</sup> uses clear, removable aligners made from advanced 3D imaging for a precise fit. No impressions are needed and patients can brush, floss and eat without bracket restrictions while progressing through staged aligners.

When orthodontic coverage applies, aligner benefits are typically covered similarly to conventional braces. We’ll review whether Invisalign<sup>®</sup> is a good fit for your goals at the initial exam.

image.alt: Close-up of clear aligners being placed on teeth

paragraphs.text: Spark and other clear aligner systems offer discreet tooth movement with custom-made trays. We begin with a fast digital scan, then design a series of aligners tailored to your tooth movements and lifestyle.

image.alt: Digital scanner used for aligner and orthodontic records

paragraphs.text: Damon self-ligating braces use a low-friction system that often feels more comfortable and can reduce treatment time for some cases. The system eliminates rubber ties, helping keep teeth and gums healthier during treatment.

image.alt: Modern dental treatment room with advanced orthodontic equipment

paragraphs.text: We perform minimally invasive tongue-tie releases with a CO2 laser to improve feeding, speech and oral function. The laser allows precise releases with minimal bleeding and typically no stitches, and most children resume normal feeding and drinking right away.
To schedule a consultation, call 908-654-4949 or request an appointment online at https://oceanswestfield.com/schedule-a-pediatric-dental-visit/.

image.alt: Patient consultation for oral surgery and laser treatment

paragraphs.text: Silver diamine fluoride is a minimally invasive option to halt early tooth decay. Applied as a topical solution for about one minute, SDF can stop progression in small cavities without drilling or sedation, making care gentler for young or anxious patients.

image.alt: Close-up dental imaging and minimally invasive treatment

paragraphs.text: Curodont is a quick, non-invasive chairside treatment that uses a proprietary peptide to promote enamel repair at early stages of decay. Treatments take minutes and can be repeated to encourage natural remineralization beneath the lesion.

paragraphs.text: Answers to common dental questions from our Westfield team, covering teething, canker sores, staining, double row teeth, and erupting molars.

This can occur in babies all the way through the college years. From their first tooth to wisdom teeth, teething can cause discomfort. Tylenol or motrin is a great option for pain relief. Cold foods, such as a frozen banana, or teether rings help our little ones. We do not recommend using Orajel with infants. Find more infant teething tips on Dr. Aimee’s baby blog where she discusses the ups and downs of her son’s teething.

Sometimes when we have a cold coming on or put our dirty fingers in our mouth we develop an ulcer or cankersore. These pesky spots can cause an immense amount of pain or sting. It usually takes a week or so to heal. It is recommended to stay away from spicy or lemony/acidic foods. Swishing with warm salt water can alleviate the discomfort and heal your mouth quicker.

If you notice you child develops dark stains on their teeth, there are many possible causes to consider. Often times iron supplements or vitamins can cause a black stain on the teeth. Some people have oral bacteria with chromogenic properties, meaning they form colors on our teeth. These stains can be easily removed with a good dental cleaning. As your child approaches teenage years they may become more concerned about the appearance and color of their teeth. At this time we can discuss whitening options such as over-the-counter white strips or in-office/at-home tray treatment.

A double row occurs when a permanent tooth grows in before the baby tooth falls out. It typically erupts behind the baby tooth, giving it the name double row. Good news, the tongue is a very strong muscle and usually once the baby tooth is out, the tongue can begin to push the permanent tooth into its rightful place. We usually start by giving the child “dentist homework” to work on getting the baby tooth out. This can mean washing hands and physically wiggling it, or biting into hard things like bagels, apples, carrots, or pizza crust. If the child is unsuccessful for about a month, we suggest giving the office a call so that Dr. Aimee can help to wiggle it out!

New molars can happen at various ages. As babies, we get our first molars around 15 months old and our second molars around 2-3 years old. As a kid we get our first permanent molars around 6 years old, our second around 12 and our third molars, AKA wisdom teeth, around 17 years old. At any of these points growing new teeth can be uncomfortable. It may require Tylenol or Motrin for discomfort. Cold stuff is great as well. For the little ones — teethers or frozen banana to gnaw on are great. For older kids, swishing with warm salt water can be helpful as the gum tissue can be a bit inflamed as that new molar breaks through. An eruption hematoma — a black and blue mark — can appear on the gums before a molar erupts. It can be tender or painful, know that once the molar comes in the black and blue will go away!
